item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

args.name: Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer

style.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical educational explainer for young kids. Bright, charming 2D cartoon animation with simple bold shapes, warm colors, friendly mood, and clear scientific visualization. A cute little orange bird stands on the left side of a grassy clearing facing a large gray cliff on the right, separated by open space. One continuous clear side-view shot with a very gentle push-in. At the beginning the bird calls out; show blue curved sound-wave arcs traveling from its beak toward the cliff, then reflecting off the rock and traveling back to the bird. Preserve the visible gap so the return is delayed: sound travels through the air, hits the cliff, and bounces back. The bird listens happily as the waves return. Use visual simplicity rather than written labels, no on-screen text. AUDIO REQUIRED: a clear, warm, friendly original narrator voice, not imitating a celebrity, speaks these exact words at an easy pace within ten seconds: 'An echo is your sound bouncing back! Shout near a cliff. Sound hits the rock and returns, so you hear it again!' Narration must be audible throughout, no music competing with the voice, and do not repeat or truncate words. Synchronize the outgoing and returning sound waves with the explanation.
